sections.html:
Montgomery is Alabama's capital and sits on the Alabama River. Residents numbered 200,603 in 2020, and the metro area counted 385,460 in 2022. The daytime population is 239,101, about 17.4% higher, because commuters fill state offices, the air force base and the hospitals each weekday.

The housing is a patchwork. You can find a downtown condo near the Capitol, a mid-century brick ranch on the east side and a farmhouse at the far edge of town, all under one city flag.

Most sellers we hear from fall into a handful of groups. Some inherited a relative's house after decades in one neighborhood. Some own a rental that has worn out faster than the rent covers. Others are moving to or from Maxwell-Gunter Air Force Base with a report date that will not wait for a long listing.

sections.h2: Who is buying and renting here
sections.html:
Government jobs keep demand steady, though they bring churn. Military families rotate on assignment cycles, and a house that misses its closing before a report date becomes a double housing cost.

Hospitals create their own pockets of demand. Baptist Medical Center South, Baptist Medical Center East near Auburn University at Montgomery, and Jackson Hospital beside Oak Park off Interstate 85 each shape the streets around them. A landlord near one of those campuses watches tenants come and go with the workday.

Families will ask which school an address feeds. Montgomery Public Schools covers most of the city and includes magnet programs. Homes on Maxwell Air Force Base are zoned separately, with a Department of Defense school for the lower grades and Montgomery Public Schools for high school.

Many of Montgomery's older neighborhoods follow the old streetcar corridors, because people moved outward along those lines. A house there can be more than a century old, so expect an inspector to study the framing, wiring and plumbing.

The city adopted a downtown master plan in 2007 for Court Square, the riverfront and Dexter Avenue, and it uses SmartCode zoning. Near downtown, the rules may differ from the outer subdivisions. Ask the city what a buyer may build or change before you promise anything.

Summers run hot. Highs pass 90 on roughly 86 days a year, and the heat index often reaches 100 by afternoon. Yearly precipitation averages about 51 inches, with February, March and July the wettest. Inspectors know this and go looking for the damage it causes:

  • Roofs bake for months, then face spring hail and wind.
  • Air conditioners work hard from May through September, so a weak unit gets flagged early.
  • Humidity averaging near 70 percent invites mold, wood rot and soft spots beneath sinks and around windows.
  • Big thunderstorms can drop hail, and weakened tropical storms can bring heavy rain.

A tornado struck the western part of the city on February 12, 1945, and storm history is still on buyers' minds. Gather roof age and any past insurance claims before you start talking.

Interstate 65 passes through town and Interstate 85 ends here. Montgomery Regional Airport flies to Atlanta, Houston and Charlotte. Passenger trains stopped running in 1995.

A short drive to an interstate ramp means quick trips to the base, downtown and the hospitals, which helps a house. A lot on a busy arterial or beside a rail line draws a lower offer from almost any buyer. Cash buyers read those traits the same way financed buyers do and subtract repair costs from what they offer.

sections.h2: Deed tax and property tax dates
sections.html:
Charge or billWho collects itAmount or date
Deed recordation taxProbate office, before the deed is recorded50 cents for each $500 of value conveyed
Annual property tax, dueCounty tax officeOctober 1
Annual property tax, delinquentCounty tax officeAfter December 31

The deed tax comes from Alabama Code section 40-22-1. The probate judge works it out from the real sale price, and you must file proof of that price on a Department of Revenue form with the deed. When a mortgage already paid its own tax, only the value above that mortgage is taxed here. Your closing attorney or title company will give you the final total, recording fee included.

Property tax is its own bill. If your sale lands in the fall, decide in the contract who pays it, since the amount is normally split by closing date. Call the Montgomery County appraisal and tax offices to get figures for your parcel and to ask about exemptions.

What to bring when you call: the parcel number or street address, and the name on the deed.

sections.h2: If you owe taxes or a mortgage
sections.html:
Owing money does not block a sale. At closing, the title company or attorney collects a payoff statement from your lender and the current tax balance from the county, then pays both from the sale proceeds before anything goes to you. The earlier you request those figures, the fewer surprises appear on the closing statement.

Liens, code fines and unpaid utility bills work the same way. They show up in the title search, and each one is paid or cleared at the table. If you are unsure what is attached to the property, ask for a title search early and read it line by line.

Heirs selling an inherited house should also gather the paperwork showing who has authority to sign. Without it, a closing cannot move forward, so start that conversation with the probate office and your attorney before you pick a date.

A cash sale fits best when the clock or the house condition is the real problem. Typical cases:

  • An inherited home whose roof or air conditioning is past repair.
  • A rental with a tenant, back rent or damage that frightens off lenders.
  • A job move for the military or the state with a hard report date.
  • A property carrying a tax bill, a code notice or another cost you want to end.

The process is brief. Send us the address and tell us about the condition. We make an offer. If you say yes, a title company or closing attorney researches the title, settles any mortgage or tax debt out of your proceeds and picks a closing day. You sign, and the money is wired at closing.

Bring a photo ID, your mortgage payoff details if you have a loan, the newest tax bill, and the lease if someone rents the house. Nothing has to be repaired or cleaned out beforehand because the purchase is as-is.

Expect an as-is offer to sit below what a fully fixed-up listing might fetch. Set it beside the likely net from a listing after repairs, commissions and the months of mortgage, taxes and utilities. We make offers on Montgomery houses, and you can always say no.

faqs.a: Yes. The seat of government moved here from Tuscaloosa on January 28, 1846. Montgomery is also the seat of Montgomery County.

faqs.q: When do Alabama property taxes come due?
faqs.a: October 1 is the due date, and the bill turns delinquent after December 31. Ask the county tax office for the exact balance and a payoff for closing.

faqs.q: What deed tax applies to a Montgomery sale?
faqs.a: The state charges 50 cents for each $500 of value conveyed, under Code section 40-22-1, and the probate office collects it before recording. A recording fee comes on top.

faqs.q: Will heat and storms affect my sale?
faqs.a: They can. Hot summers, hail and heavy rain age roofs, cooling systems and crawl spaces, and inspectors look there first. A cash sale lets you skip fixing them.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Montgomery house that needs work?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers take houses in current condition, whether the problem is an old roof, water damage or years of deferred upkeep. The offer accounts for the work.
